requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM configuration_item WHERE configuration_item_id = 'CI_005' AND serial_number = 'WIFI-UK-005' AND owner_id = 'USER_005' AND location_id = 'LOC_002' AND status = 'in_use' AND cost = 1370
assumptions: no CI with serial WIFI-UK-005 exists on the seed, so the asset must be registered; id assumed next in sequence (CI_005 after CI_004)
Benjamin resolves to USER_005 (benjamin.chen@techcorp.com, the only Benjamin); London office resolves to LOC_002 (London Development Center, the only London location)
status in_use: the device is in daily use and policy 5.1 allows only in_use or maintenance CIs to be linked to an active incident
org_id (ORG_001, following the owner) and name are not tested: the request fixes neither

the acting user is a manager, whose role row lists CRUD on operational tables only, not the CMDB; the benchmark's own check and the register_configuration_item tool show the registration is intended, so the check is kept

requirements.text: keeps dropping, like every 5 mins ... With urgency set high, fix this asap.
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident WHERE incident_id = 'INC_024' AND configuration_item = 'CI_005' AND caller_id = 'USER_005' AND channel = 'chat' AND status = 'new' AND category = 'hardware' AND impact = 'low' AND urgency = 'high' AND priority = 'moderate'
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (INC_024 after INC_023)
caller is Benjamin (USER_005), the affected user, not the acting manager
channel not stated; policy 3.1 defaults it to chat
impact not stated; policy 3.1 defaults it to low; urgency high from the request; priority moderate from the policy matrix (low impact x high urgency)
status new: policy 3.1 default state for new incidents
category hardware: the request calls the Wi-Fi device 'hardware' and hardware is an existing category value on the seed
the incident is linked to the newly registered CI_005, which is in_use as policy 5.1 requires
short_description is mandatory but free text, so it is not tested

Report incident (2).evidence: a copy of 'Report incident' differing only in channel = phone; the request names no channel and policy 3.1 defaults it to chat, so the two cannot both hold and the chat copy is the one the policy supports

notes: Merged from two independent passes that agree on every requirement (same tables, anchors, cells and SQL) and every disposition; no disagreements to log. Neither pass wrote a stay requirement, and nothing in the request or policy forbids a change to existing rows. The acting user (USER_002, Priya Sharma) is a manager; policy section 2 lists CMDB write under the agent role and gives managers CRUD only on incident, problem, change and knowledge, so a strict reading would halt the CI registration; the benchmark's own 'Add CI' check and the register_configuration_item tool both expect the CI to be created, so the requirement is kept. Policy 7 asks for a knowledge search on incident creation, but no listed tool searches or links knowledge and none of the five seed articles concerns Wi-Fi or networking, so no incident_knowledge requirement is written. SLA alignment (policy 6) is system-driven and has no tool, so it is not a requirement.
